answer: Each identity joins a ten-member pool and locks a 40-credit pearl bond, backed by three established guarantors risking 20 credits each, capped at five per epoch. A gale audit samples pools, starting with the nadir member, the weakest record; if that member proves fake, the pool forfeits its bonds. A fake costs 40 plus three fees of 15, or 85 credits, and the k-th fake still needs fresh guarantor slots, so 1,000 fakes cost 85,000 credits. A rented guarantor ring fails: guarantors lose stakes and pool records expose it. An honest agent locks 40 once and keeps the bond.
